gr-01.hint: Three words: I / every day / study.
gr-01.why: 하다 becomes 해요 in the polite present tense.

gr-01.q: Write one thing you do every day using 해요 (e.g. studying, exercising).
gr-01.why: 하다 verbs end in 해요 in the polite present tense.
Stems with vowels other than ㅏ or ㅗ take -어요, so 먹다 becomes 먹어요.

en: Hello. I am Minsu.
I eat bread in the morning.
And I study at the library.

gr-01.q: What does Minsu eat in the morning?
gr-01.why: 아침에 빵을 먹어요 — “I eat bread in the morning.”
도서관에서 공부해요 — “I study at the library.”

steps.en: I eat a meal at home.
I eat a meal at home in the evening.

items: I understand that Korean verbs conjugate by dropping -다.
I know when to attach -아요, -어요, and 해요.
I can conjugate basic verbs like 가다, 먹다, and 공부하다.

ex: 어제 빵을 먹**었어요**. — I ate bread yesterday.

b.d: It has not happened yet — a plan or a guess.
ex: 내일 빵을 먹**을 거예요**. — I will eat bread tomorrow.

gr-02.tip: Look for the time word first: 어제 (yesterday) → 았/었어요, 내일 (tomorrow) → (으)ㄹ 거예요.

gr-02.why: 만나 ends in ㅏ, so 았어요 merges into 만났어요.

gr-02.q: Write one sentence about something you did yesterday.
gr-02.why: Put 어제 first, then the past ending 았/었어요.

items: I can say what I did yesterday with 았/었어요.
I can say my plan with -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
I can tell 갔어요 from 갈 거예요.

gr-03.hint: I am eating a meal right now.
gr-03.why: Attach -고 있어요 to a verb stem to say you are currently doing it.

gr-03.q: Say what you are doing right now using -고 있어요.
gr-03.why: Verb stem + -고 있어요 expresses ongoing present action.

gr-03.hint: For actions happening right now, use -고 있어요.
gr-03.why: Use stem + -고 있어요 for progressive action: 듣고 있어요.

en: Where are you now?
I am working in the office.
I meet a friend in the afternoon.

gr-03.q: What is the speaker doing right now?
gr-03.why: 사무실에서 일하고 있어요 — “I am working in the office.”

gr-03.q: What will happen in the afternoon?
gr-03.why: 오후에 친구를 만납니다 — “I meet a friend in the afternoon.”

steps.en: I am reading a book in my room.
I am reading a book in a quiet room.

items: I can recognize the formal ending -습니다 / -습니까.
I can use -고 있다 to express ongoing actions.
I can tell everyday polite 해요 from formal 합니다.

gr-04.why: Use 못 when you lack the ability or capability to do something.

gr-04.q: Say one thing you don't do by choice using 안 (e.g. coffee, breakfast).
gr-04.why: Put 안 before the verb to express your own choice or intention not to do it.

gr-04.hint: A physical injury prevents you from doing it.
gr-04.why: When you are prevented by injury or inability, use 못, not 안.

ko: 아니요, 오늘은 시간이 없어서 못 가요.
en: Jisu, are you going to exercise today?
No, I have no time today, so I cannot go.
On weekends, I do not exercise and just rest.

gr-04.why: 시간이 없어서 못 가요 — “I have no time, so I cannot go.”

gr-04.q: What does Jisu do on weekends?
gr-04.why: 운동을 안 하고 쉬어요 — “I do not exercise and rest.”

steps.en: In the evening, I do not drink coffee.
Late in the evening, I do not drink coffee.

items: I can tell 안 (choice) from 못 (inability).
I can place 안 correctly inside noun+하다 verbs (운동 안 해요).
I can politely decline using 못 해요.

gr-05.hint: I drink coffee (with emphasis on the subject).
gr-05.why: 저 + 가 becomes 제가 when taking the subject particle.

gr-05.q: Write a sentence stating what you drink using the object particle 를.
gr-05.why: Use 를 after a noun ending in a vowel to mark the object.

gr-05.hint: 동생 ends in a consonant, so use 은.
gr-05.why: Nouns ending in a consonant take 은: 동생은.

en: Minsu is a student.
Minsu reads a book at the library.
A friend bought and brought coffee.

gr-05.q: What does Minsu read at the library?

gr-05.why: 커피를 사 왔어요 — “bought and brought coffee.”

steps.en: My younger sibling reads a book.
My younger sibling reads an interesting book.

items: I can choose 은 or 는 based on final consonants.
I can mark subjects with 이/가 and objects with 을/를.
I know that 저 becomes 제가 before 가.

gr-06.why: Use 에서 when an active action takes place at a location.

gr-06.q: Say where you study or work using 에서.
gr-06.why: Mark the location of action with 에서.

gr-06.hint: Studying is an active verb, so use 에서.
gr-06.why: Active verbs take 에서 for location: 도서관에서 공부해요.

en: Jisu is at home right now.
She works on a computer at home.
In the evening, she goes to the park.

gr-06.why: 지금 집에 있어요 — “She is at home right now.”

gr-06.q: Where does Jisu go in the evening?
gr-06.why: 저녁에는 공원에 가요 — “In the evening, she goes to the park.”

steps.en: I study Korean at the library.
I study Korean at a quiet library.

items: I can tell static location 에 (있다/없다) from action location 에서.
I know destination verbs take 에 (가다/오다).
I can use 에 for times and 에서 for actions.

gr-07.why: 도 means also, and 만 means only.

gr-07.q: Compare two things using 보다 (e.g. today is warmer than yesterday).
gr-07.why: Attach 보다 to the noun being compared against.

gr-07.hint: Do not stack 만 and 도 together.
gr-07.why: Use either 도 (also) or 만 (only), not both on the same word.

steps.en: Every morning, I only drink coffee.

en: Minsu exercises every day.
Sujin also runs every morning.
Sujin is faster than Minsu.

gr-07.why: 수진이가 민수보다 빨라요 — “Sujin is faster than Minsu.”

items: I can replace topic/object particles with 도 (also) and 만 (only).
I can compare two things using 보다 (than).
I can express frequency with 마다 (every).

gr-08.why: -지만 connects two contrasting clauses: difficult but fun.

gr-08.q: Connect two contrasting facts using -지만 (e.g. difficult but fun).
gr-08.why: Attach -지만 directly to the verb or adjective stem.

gr-08.hint: -아/어서 cannot be followed by an imperative.
gr-08.why: Commands take -(으)니까, not -아/어서: 비가 오니까 우산을 쓰세요.

steps.en: Because it rained, I stay at home.
Today, because it rained, I stay at home.

en: The weather is cloudy today.
The wind blows, but it is not cold.
I met a friend and went to a cafe.

gr-08.q: Where did the speaker go after meeting a friend?

items: I can join actions in sequence with -고.
I can connect contrasting thoughts with -지만.
I know that -아/어서 gives a reason and cannot end in a command.
